archetypes.name: bash-state
archetypes.rationale: The diff adds shell-state transitions that can accidentally clear OOS_PENDING or permit PR creation before OOS disposition is visible.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the shell state transitions around step2-implement.sh, ship-pr.sh pr-prep, oos-disposition-checkpoint.sh, and OOS_PENDING. Pay close attention to non-zero helper exits, set -e interactions, state_set ordering, fork/repo-unavailable carve-outs, and whether PR creation can proceed while manifest OOS remains only in JSON. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: manifest-materializer
archetypes.rationale: The new materialize-manifest-oos.sh helper is the mechanical bridge for manifest-only OOS and has many parsing/idempotency edge cases.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect materialize-manifest-oos.sh for jq extraction, title normalization, monotonic OOS_N allocation, duplicate-title idempotency, multi-line descriptions, security routing, and redaction behavior. Check that malformed or partial inputs fail closed only where intended and that helper outputs match the documented markdown contracts. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: python-bash-parity
archetypes.rationale: The Python ship path must mirror bash ship-pr behavior for design-OOS resolution and pre-gate manifest materialization.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare python/ship.py and its tests against scripts/ship-pr.sh for accepted design-OOS path resolution, materialize-manifest-oos invocation timing, failure handling, and NEEDS_USER_OOS_FILING routing. Look for semantic drift between bash and Python around design-export fallback, runner subprocess usage, and when PR creation is blocked. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: log-evidence
archetypes.rationale: The OOS pipeline changes alter sentinel recovery, NDJSON evidence, duplicate dispositions, and run-statistics ownership.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review oos-pipeline.md and SKILL.md changes for the larch-log evidence contract across normal filing, duplicate issue disposition, sentinel recovery, all-already-filed design batches, partial /issue failure, and rejected OOS entries. Verify that run-statistics remains post-checkpoint-only and that no failed or partial filing path can satisfy the disposition gate with accepted URL rows. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: public-redaction
archetypes.rationale: Manifest OOS data is copied into public issue/log surfaces and private security breadcrumbs with redaction-sensitive boundaries.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace manifest-derived titles, descriptions, focus areas, worksheets, issue bodies, larch-log records, execution-issues breadcrumbs, and security-oos-observations for redaction and disclosure boundaries. Check whether secrets, PII, internal URLs, or security-routed details can leak to public or committed surfaces, including through titles and warning entries. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: grep-guards
archetypes.rationale: The new structure assertions rely on fixed-string and scoped grep/awk checks that can be brittle or falsely reassuring.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review scripts/test-implement-structure.sh and Makefile harness wiring for brittle fixed-string assertions, incorrectly scoped negative checks, awk range extraction mistakes, shard registration drift, and tests that can pass while the contract is still broken. Focus on whether the guards actually enforce ordering, load-directive placement, sentinel pins, redaction pins, and manifest materialization hooks without over-constraining harmless wording. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
